title: QBR - StratusRetail health check
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost optimization levers, reliability incidents over last quarter, and roadmap alignment for StratusRetail's personalization and search features. Customer is exploring a Dedicated pool for predictable latency and cost; asked for benchmarks and security artefacts. Agreed next steps: pricing proposal, SOC2/ISO docs, run dedicated benchmark, and a technical deep dive on quantization and batching.
next_steps: Maya to send updated pricing and committed usage discount proposal by 2025-12-02
Ethan to schedule Dedicated pool benchmark and share runbook by 2025-12-05
Priya to provide sample traffic shape (1 week of p95/p99) and SLOs by 2025-12-01
Lina to follow up with onboarding checklist and success plan by 2025-12-04
action_items: Maya Chen - send pricing and committed usage proposal - due 2025-12-02
Ethan Park - run dedicated pool benchmark, share results and runbook - due 2025-12-05
Priya Shah - provide sample traffic shape and desired SLOs - due 2025-12-01
Lina Gomez - follow up on onboarding checklist and coordinate kickoff - due 2025-12-04
transcript: Header: 2025-11-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM); Oliver Grant (StratusRetail Head of AI), Priya Shah (Eng Manager), Marco Diaz (SRE)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR — big thanks to Oliver and team for making time. Quick agenda: usage/cost review, reliability incidents, roadmap alignment, and next steps. We'll keep this tight to 45-ish minutes.
[01:12] Oliver Grant: Yeah thanks Maya. Busy quarter, appreciate you folks. We'll start with a quick look at numbers then dig into the two outages in Sept we saw and the latency spikes last month.

[02:05] Lina Gomez: Quick note — I shared the QBR deck and the usage sheet in the chat, link: drive.redwood/qbr/stratus-2025-q4. Also the SOC2 docs are in the security folder, will re-share after the call.

[03:10] Priya Shah: sounds good. On usage: our token consumption is up about 42% q/q, mostly from the recommender endpoint. Cost is up accordingly, and the team is trying to decide if we move to Dedicated or use more batching/quant profiles.

[04:20] Ethan Park: On batching/quant, we saw 20-30% unit cost reduction on some ecom workloads using int8 quant and smarter batching with prefix cache. That said, tail latency can be trickier if you push too much batching for low-latency routes.

[05:00] Marco Diaz: Right — our p99 for personalization bumped from 320ms to 480ms during peak on Black Friday sim. We need predictable tails, which is why Dedicated looks attractive. But we need to understand cost and failure modes.

[06:30] Maya Chen: Totally. For Dedicated, the primary benefits are reserved GPU pools for throughput predictability, isolation for tenancy, and configurable autoscaling policies. We can do a canary start — small pool — and measure.
[07:45] Oliver Grant: Can you run a benchmark with our workload shape? We want to see p50/p95/p99 and token cost under steady and bursty patterns.

[08:30] Ethan Park: Yes, we'll need sample traffic: RPS, typical sequence length distribution, and failure tolerance. Priya, if you can drop the last week's traffic shape that will help. We'll run both Hosted and Dedicated sims and share a results spreadsheet.
[09:10] Priya Shah: I'll export the p95/p99 histograms and send. One question: will the Dedicated pool give us automatic KMS integration? We need HSM-backed keys for some PCI-adjacent flows.

[09:50] Maya Chen: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations — we'll include the exact docs. Also RBAC and audit logs for every token-level access are available in the Private offerings, but Dedicated has strong audit hooks too.
[11:20] Oliver Grant: How about SSO and SAML for console access? Our security team asks for SAML + SCIM and tight session controls.
[11:40] Lina Gomez: Yes, Redwood Console supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; we'll attach the SSO implement guide. Also, we can offer longer retention on audit logs as an add-on if needed.

[13:05] Marco Diaz: There were two incidents in Sept — one caused by an injector bug in our app, one where models fell back to a slower variant under capacity. Can you describe the fallback policy mechanics? Sometimes fallback spawns cold-start latency.

[14:10] Ethan Park: Sure, smart routing will route by policy — region, latency, cost tier — and when capacity's constrained we can failover to compatible quantized variants. We also do warm pool strategies to reduce cold starts; but yes, transitions can add tail. We can tune canary/rollout and pre-warm the KV cache to mitigate.

[15:55] Oliver Grant: You mentioned KV cache — last time our notes read K-V cash in the transcript, haha, so yes please pre-warm. Also curious about model upgrades: we plan to test a new open-research model in Jan — what is the best rollout pattern?

[17:00] Maya Chen: For model rollouts we recommend staged canary (1-5-20-100%), eval sets and regen tests, and automated rollback on quality regressions. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching profiles for that model shape too.
[18:40] Priya Shah: On quality regressions — do you have an automated alert if a metric (e.g., click-through on A/B prompt) degrades after a deploy? We want guardrails.
[19:05] Lina Gomez: Yes, we can set up evaluation suites and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; those can trigger rollbacks or notify the oncall.
[20:30] Oliver Grant: Back to cost. If we commit to a monthly reserved capacity, what kind of discount are we looking at? We're trying to present a cost model to finance.

[21:00] Maya Chen: Typical reserved discounts scale with commit size and term. For a 12-month commit at your current baseline + 30% buffer we'd expect X-20% to Y-35% range — I'll put precise numbers in the proposal. Also, model quantization can reduce per-token compute by ~25% in many cases.
[22:15] Marco Diaz: Will quantization impact output quality for our ranking prompts? We need to test end-to-end.
[22:40] Ethan Park: It can, depends on prompt sensitivity. We'll run A/B regressions on your test set — usually negligible degradation with int8 for many architectures, but we always validate.
[24:05] Priya Shah: For the benchmark, can you simulate the Black Friday traffic pattern? That's the main worry — sudden bursts and mixed short/long requests.
[24:45] Ethan Park: Yes we'll run two sims: steady-state and bursty (k-surge) with warm-up phases. We'll include p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens at both points.
[26:20] Oliver Grant: Also curious — what's the failure domain for Dedicated? If a GPU node fails, what's our recovery time?

[26:45] Maya Chen: Dedicated pools have multi-AZ placement and automatic instance replacement; recovery depends on pre-warmed caches. For strict SLOs we recommend reserved + warm pools and a small burst capacity in another region as fallback.
[28:10] Oliver Grant: Sounds good. Security doc ask again — SOC2 and ISO certs plus any pen-test results if you have them.
[28:35] Lina Gomez: Will re-share SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 cert, and a redacted pen-test summary. Also, we'll include the audit log retention and encryption details (KMS/HSM) in the package.
[30:00] Priya Shah: One more operational question: when you say 'prefix cache' — how is that different from session/KV cache? We have sticky sessions and want to avoid duplicated compute.

[30:30] Ethan Park: Prefix caching caches repeated request prefixes to avoid recompute; KV cache is more about key-value activations for autoregressive decoders. Both help, but prefix cache is often very effective for templated prompts.
[31:40] Oliver Grant: Any notable outages last quarter on Redwood side? We logged two external-facing issues during a region failover — what was root cause?

[32:10] Maya Chen: There was a regional network event that increased tail latency for some hosted endpoints; we fell back to other regions for some customers. We've added better routing heuristics and pre-warm heuristics since then. We'll share the postmortem.
[33:45] Marco Diaz: Appreciate the PM. For our pilot do you recommend Hosted first or spin up a small Dedicated cluster?

[34:10] Ethan Park: Hosted is fastest; Dedicated gives predictability. Recommend staged approach: continue Hosted for non-critical features, run a pilot Dedicated pool for personalization, measure, then decide commit size.
[35:25] Priya Shah: What's the timeline for onboarding Dedicated if we sign a 12-month commit?
[35:50] Maya Chen: From contract sign to live Dedicated pool typically 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and networking (VPC peering, KMS setup). Private/on-prem takes longer.
[36:40] Oliver Grant: Ok. Let's recap next steps before we close.

[36:55] Maya Chen: Recap: we'll send pricing and committed usage numbers; Ethan will run the Dedicated benchmark with your traffic; Priya will send traffic sample; Lina will reshare SOC2 and SSO docs and follow onboarding checklist. Any additions?
[38:10] Priya Shah: We'll also give a list of deployment owners and oncall contacts for the bench run.
[39:25] Oliver Grant: Good. One more thing — do you support cross-region failover with session affinity? That was a pain point last time.

[39:50] Ethan Park: We support cross-region routing but session affinity across regions is tricky; we recommend sticky tokens and a warm standby region. We'll include architecture notes in the runbook.
[41:00] Lina Gomez: I'll open the follow-up email after this call with a summary and links to the docs referenced (QBR deck, SOC2, SSO guide, benchmark template).
[41:25] Maya Chen: Great — any final questions?
[42:00] Oliver Grant: none from me. Thank you all. Looking forward to the benchmark results.
[43:15] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll aim to have the proposal and initial bench plan by next week. Talk soon.
[45:00] Meeting ended: 15:47 UTC
